quotes.text: The tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record, so any task can be traced back to its origin

rationale: The paper names the dataset (MIMIC-IV), version 2.2, a snapshot date, the platform (PhysioNet), and a route from each task to its source patient record. All four anchor elements are present. Note that Appendix A.3 describes the records as collected 2008-2019, which is a different time frame description.

quotes.text: The source database consists of de-identified patient records collected between 2008 and 2019 from routine hospital care.
Distribution follows a credentialed data use agreement, and the originating institution's IRB approved a consent waiver for this research.

rationale: Origin, collection method (routine hospital care), terms (credentialed DUA) and IRB consent waiver are all stated. Note: Appendix Z states a MIT code licence while the README states Apache-2.0; this repo-licence inconsistency is recorded but does not lower the score.

quotes.text: we compared the age, sex and race distribution of the benchmark patients against the U.S. adult inpatient population

rationale: Appendix Z reports a comparison of age, sex and race distributions against a named target population (U.S. adult inpatient population from a national hospital discharge survey), with differences under five percentage points.

searched: S1 (paper, appendices incl. Appendix Z), S2 (README), S3 (no chunks), S4, S5 (no chunks). No dedicated unsafe-output or bias test is reported on S1-S3. The only mention is a comment in S4 agent_eval/notes.py, and code comments never count as reporting (G1a).

quotes.text: Contamination mitigation includes gating access to the test split.
Measurement of verbatim overlap with public web corpora revealed zero exact matches between test tasks and public sources.

rationale: A developer-side control (gated test split, plus a held-out split and canary string elsewhere) is paired with a measured verbatim-overlap check reporting zero exact matches. Note: the README says there is no separate test-set release and the held-out task ids are public, which tensions with gating.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: Isolation is stated with named mechanisms (separate evaluation service, no network path, labels not published in the repository). Note: the README caveat says that under SkyRL's pinned Harbor 0.1.44 the agent runs as root and could read the answer key in /var/lib/caa; this is an S2 disclosure, not code, so no contradiction flag is set.

quotes.text: Environment components are fixed at release: database snapshot, software image, and patient-simulation LLM are each version-pinned.
During evaluation, only the model under test is called; no other external services are involved.

contradiction_quotes.text: During evaluation, only the model under test is called; no other external services are involved.
no API key is written anywhere: patient and judge go through klinikebench_train.keyproxy on the host.

rationale: The paper reports data, software image and simulator pinned with no external call other than the model under test, which meets the anchor for 2. Code and README show patient and judge LLM calls through a live proxy to an external endpoint at evaluation time, which is a candidate contradiction to verify.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader and the result is reported. Note: the reported count of 120 differs from the 333 tasks in the benchmark.

quotes.text: The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged

rationale: Tasks change state (orders, prescriptions, referrals), so the item applies. The paper states the grader checks unchanged as well as changed state, with out-of-scope modifications counted as failures.

quotes.text: Random-action agents achieve 3.1% success across tasks.

rationale: An empirical random-agent success rate is reported (3.1%), and Appendix Z reports a random agent at 2.5% and a do-nothing agent at 0.0%. Note the two random-agent figures differ.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks, and a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks.
Random-action agents achieve 3.1% success across tasks.

rationale: Do-nothing and random agent scores are reported, stated as covering all tasks (the 3.1% random figure is across tasks). Caveat: the do-nothing result is given for 120 tasks while the benchmark has 333, so full coverage is only clear for the random-agent figure.

quotes.text: We validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%

rationale: The benchmark validates its own automatic evaluator on 200 physician-labelled outputs with agreement, false-positive (3%) and false-negative (8%) rates. Appendix Z adds a grader validation on 150 injected outcomes.

quotes.text: For each model, five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7.
Patient simulation uses temperature 0.7 and history judging uses temperature 0.

rationale: Seeds, temperatures and a repeated-run policy (five independent runs, mean reported) are stated in S1. Note inconsistencies: Section 3.1 says one rollout per model-task pair, Appendix Z says temperature 0, and an S4 comment claims temperature 0 with three runs; the S4 comment does not count as reporting.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)

rationale: Bootstrap 95% CIs for all model scores and a paired permutation test of the difference between the two best models are reported, which covers the headline comparison.

quotes.text: For each model, five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7.

rationale: Run count (five per task, averaged), seed and temperature policy, and independence are all stated. Note: Section 3.1 states one rollout per model-task pair, which conflicts with the five-run statement.

quotes.text: Headline scores carry 95% bootstrap CIs where the resampling unit is the task.
the bootstrap resamples patients to address within-patient clustering

rationale: CIs on headline scores, the resampling unit (task), and handling of within-patient clustering via patient resampling are all stated.

quotes.text: We report pass^8 (share of tasks solved in all 8 runs) and agreement rates of the final environment state across these eight runs.

rationale: A pass^8 all-runs metric and final-state agreement across eight reruns are reported with the run count. No action-sequence agreement is reported, so element (i) is false.

quotes.text: using the snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0
Medium reasoning effort is used across all models.

rationale: Snapshot identifiers, decoding parameters (including reasoning effort) and a harness release tied to the reported numbers are stated. Caveats: snapshot IDs are given for only two models (one not in the evaluated list), and temperature 0 here conflicts with 0.7 in the main text.

quotes.text: The agent discovers tools through clinic tools , which returns their names, descriptions, and JSON parameter schemas.
Write tools update the simulated encounter: laboratory and imaging orders receive identifiers, while prescriptions, referrals, admissions, and plans are stored as structured records.
Knowledge-graph query tools and their aliases return not_available in the headless runtime.

rationale: JSON parameter schemas, read versus write behaviour per tool group (Table 5, B.2), and return semantics including not_available and daemon rejections are documented. Whether the read/write distinction reaches the agent-visible tool descriptions cannot be told from the packet (S5 has no chunks).

quotes.text: Conformance testing confirms tool behavior matches documentation.
Two tools consist of simulated stubs providing fixed placeholder responses.
This is disclosed both in the paper and in the tool descriptions visible to the agent.

rationale: Conformance testing and a dispatch audit are reported, stubbed or mocked behaviour is disclosed (Appendix B.2 also lists mocked results), and the paper states the disclosure appears in agent-visible tool descriptions. The S5 reach rests on the paper's statement because no S5 chunks are in the packet.

quotes.text: Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.
The agent prompt states that writes are sandboxed.
Write tools update the simulated encounter: laboratory and imaging orders receive identifiers, while prescriptions, referrals, admissions, and plans are stored as structured records.

rationale: Write actions (orders, prescriptions, referrals, notes) are identified, their sandboxed execution is stated, and unsafe or unnecessary writes are penalised. The paper states the agent prompt discloses sandboxing; S5 itself is not in the packet.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.
We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: Grader input is stated (final environment state) and it is validated on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates. Elsewhere the paper grades transcripts and tool traces with an LLM judge, and no rationale for that is given, so element (ii) is marked false.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: Leakage controls (no web access, restricted retrieval), a private held-out split with hidden labels, and a canary string are all stated. Note: the README says the 50 held-out tasks are public with listed ids and there is no separate test-set release.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race
each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: Results per task family and per sex and race subgroup are reported with case counts per slice, as stated in Appendix Z. The packet does not show the slice tables themselves.

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.
the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence

rationale: Source is stated as real de-identified records, governance is stated (credentialed DUA, safe harbour de-identification, IRB waiver), and data terms are stated separately from the code licence. Note: the README lists Apache-2.0 while Appendix Z mentions an MIT code licence.
